A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ModalTune study. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the methods, equations, tables, and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original TCGA cancer-subtyping and survival experiments, OOD evaluations, ablations, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds linear-probing controls, further ablations, TITAN experiments, and clinical-input experiments.

M1.justification: The original Modal Adapter, task prompts, feature fusion, text targets, and KL objective remain unchanged. v2 adds a clinical-input extension using a two-layer MLP to produce a token concatenated with transcriptomics features (Supplementary Section 13), and instantiates the framework with TITAN.

E1.justification: The same six TCGA cohorts and the same subtyping and survival tasks remain. Supplementary Section 13 adds an input scenario using clinical covariates alongside WSIs and transcriptomics; the TITAN experiments introduce no additional cohort or prediction task.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens the controls: Gigapath linear probing joins both in-domain and OOD comparisons in Tables 2–3; Table 8 adds LoRA and ABMIL with text embeddings; Tables 9 and 11 introduce TITAN linear-probing, tuning, and fusion comparators. The original comparator rows are retained.

E3.justification: New evaluation configurations include pretrained-feature linear probing, TITAN-specific re-extraction of patch features, and controlled adapter, text-training, and clinical-input variants. The existing patient splits, balanced-accuracy/C-index metrics, and original training settings remain unchanged. These are additions to the evaluation design, not documented revisions of the original experiments.

E4.justification: v2 adds tests of adapter choice using LoRA, whether text-based multitask training benefits ABMIL, transferability to TITAN, and the value of additional clinical inputs. These substantially extend validation of the framework's design and extensibility. The original ablations and qualitative analyses remain, although v1's untabulated observation about single-task text targets is removed.

E5.justification: The stated three-seed mean/standard-deviation reporting and median-risk Kaplan–Meier analysis with a log-rank threshold of 0.05 are unchanged. New trained-model rows follow the existing uncertainty format; no increased run count or new statistical procedure is reported.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results in Tables 2, 3, 7, and 8 are unchanged, but numerous results are added. Table 9 reports ModalTune TITAN overall balanced accuracy/C-index of 0.942/0.735. Table 10 reports 0.950/0.755 for the clinical-input variant versus 0.954/0.750 for the retained default. These and the new baseline and ablation rows expand the evidence rather than improve the original scores.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(5) are retained. Supplementary Section 11.5 preserves the same random-projection and Johnson–Lindenstrauss reasoning; no new theorem, proof, or substantive derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 removes a central claimed benefit: mitigating catastrophic forgetting disappears from the abstract, introduction's stated challenges and contributions, and conclusion. The conclusion also drops the specific rare-disease applicability claim. The unified multimodal, multitask, pan-cancer contribution and overall performance claims remain.

C2.justification: v2 removes the speculative forgetting/overfitting explanation for performance gains and qualifies untested modality extensions as possible in principle. New discussion links text-training benefits to architecture and attributes the RCC clinical-input degradation to potentially less relevant clinical features. The original computational-cost and convergence limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 supplies a public-code repository link, newly specifies HSV thresholding for foreground patch selection, and documents the clinical covariates and their two-layer encoder. HSV thresholding is newly disclosed rather than established as a changed procedure. The shared hyperparameter table is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds the LoRA reference and removes the Alfasly et al. retrieval and de Jong et al. medical-center robustness references while narrowing the introduction's motivation. The related-work survey largely remains intact. The additional CLIP bibliography entry duplicates a work already cited in v1.

P1.justification: Targeted rewrites affect the abstract, introduction, selected method and results passages, and conclusion. Two supplementary sections are inserted, moving Qualitative Analysis from Section 12 to Section 14. Affiliation and terminology edits accompany these changes, while the overall narrative structure remains stable.

P2.justification: Tables 2, 3, and 8 gain rows, and Tables 9–11 are added using the existing presentation style. Captions, sizing, and float placement receive limited adjustments. All six figures retain identical underlying artwork, including the relocated appendix visualizations.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps through pretrained linear-probing controls, alternative-adapter comparisons, and direct tests of another slide encoder and additional clinical inputs. Removing the unsupported catastrophic-forgetting claim also improves the match between claims and evidence. Section 12 nevertheless overstates the TITAN OOD advantage over the next-best baseline by overlooking the stronger linear-probing comparator in Table 11. Despite that qualification, the added controls and extensibility tests substantially strengthen the paper.
